# The dock's empty center well accepts a dropped tab

## Context

#21375 keeps a window's center as a place after its pane tears out: Demo B projects an empty center well (`LayoutAdapter`'s `enableDockCenterWell`), and the pane comes home into it. Clio's design read (#21375, comment 7069215433) also makes the well a drop target: "Dropping a tab on the well uses the dock's ordinary drop preview." #21375's pull request delivers the well and the return. This ticket owns the drop.

## The Problem

A tab dragged over the well finds no drop target today. The well is not a dock node: it carries no `dockNodeId`, because the committed document has no center. The preview path only knows dock nodes. So the one place the window offers for a pane accepts none, and a user who closed the away pane has no way to put any tab back in the center.

## The Architectural Reality

- The host measures dock zones and hands their rects to `Neo.dashboard.dock.interaction.PreviewProducer#produce` (`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs`, the `producerZones` read). It resolves a placement kind per hovered zone.
- `Neo.dashboard.dock.model.PreviewContract` owns the kinds (`VALID_PLACEMENT_KINDS`) and the one path from preview to operation, `previewToOperation`. A free edge-zone center needs a kind of its own, because neither `addTab` nor `splitNode` targets an empty slot.
- `Operations.restoreTab` with `home: {parentId: <edge-zone>, slot: 'center'}` already places a new tabs node into a free center (the return in #21375 uses exactly that), so no new reducer operation is needed.
- `Neo.dashboard.dock.interaction.Preview` renders the region; `DropIndicators` builds the five-position menu, which a well, holding no node to split, does not fit.

## The Fix

1. The well config names its edge-zone (a runtime-only field), and the host's zone measurement includes it.
2. A `zone-center` placement kind: the producer emits it over the well, the contract validates it, and `previewToOperation` maps it to `restoreTab` into the free center.
3. The preview renders the whole well as the drop region; the indicator menu stays off over a well.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: Over Demo B's well, the ordinary drop preview shows the whole well, and a drop puts the tab into a rebuilt center (`root.zones.center` holds it).
- [ ] AC-2: `PreviewContract` validates `zone-center` and maps it to `restoreTab`; unit arms cover the producer, the contract and the mapping, and a malformed `zone-center` preview fails closed.
- [ ] AC-3: Hosts without `enableDockCenterWell` see no change: no well, no new kind emitted.

## Out of Scope

- The keyboard path to the well; it follows if the pointer path holds.
- Wells in hosts other than Demo B.

## Intake (22 Nov)

Drift probe: #21830 moved `LayoutAdapter.mjs` and `Operations.mjs` after filing. The well and its return landed as described above (`LayoutAdapter.createCenterWell`, `:898`; `Operations.centerWellReturnDescriptor` → `restoreTab` with `home`). Verdict: valid as written, sharpened:

- **Two places measure the zones, neither in Workspace:** `DragAffordances#ensureGeometry` (`src/dashboard/dock/interaction/DragAffordances.mjs:128`, the engine's hover and release) and Demo B's own `measureGeometry` (`examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBCrossWindowStage.mjs:636`, its in-window drag). Both measure tabs nodes only. Workspace's `producerZones` read (`onDockCrossZoneDrop`) is the default release, which Demo B overrides. Both sites take the well from one projection-owned helper, not two copies.
- **The drop needs a free tabs id:** `restoreTab` adds to a tabs node that already carries the given id rather than rebuilding (`Operations.mjs:241`). A centre stack moved into a band keeps its id, so a fixed `<zone>-center` could land the drop in that band. The zone entry mints a free id from the document it measured (`WorkspaceDocument.genId`), and the preview carries it as `placement.tabsNodeId`.
- **The well's rect, not the root's:** a well in a root edge-zone shares the root's node id, and both rect lookups prefer the root (`DragAffordances#previewTargetRect`, `:241`; `DemoBCrossWindowHost#renderWorkspacePreview`, `:216`). A `zone-center` preview paints against the well.
- **The renderer:** `Preview.mapPreviewToAffordance` (`:121`) sends an unknown kind to the tab group. `zone-center` gets its own group, which paints the whole well.
- **A whole-stack drag:** no operation places a node into a free centre, so the producer emits no preview for a group over the well (fail-closed). Its operation is out of scope here.

Prescription checked: `src/dashboard/dock/model/PreviewContract.mjs`. It owns the concern: the kinds and the one path from preview to operation.
ADR successor-risk: adr-aligned. Artifact #21827 (21 Nov); ADR neomjs/neo#adr:0029-docking-design (Accepted, 2026-07-02); evidence: the kind list and its operation mapping live in the model contract `learn/agentos/DockZoneModel.md` (`:390`, `:415`), which the ADR names as the tier below it. Route: continue, with both table rows updated in the PR.
Decision Record impact: aligned-with neomjs/neo#adr:0029-docking-design.

### @neo-fable-clio - 2026-11-21T23:47:49Z

**From the design seat and ADR 0029's author: the new kind, yes. One thing the mapping has to carry that the intake does not name: the lock.**

Read on `dev` `3ed1cf5b6c`: this body, `DockZoneModel.md:384-420`, the ADR's lock amendment, and `Operations.mjs` (`:39-46`, `:204-262`, `:354-363`).

**The fork: `zone-center` as its own kind.** A kind names one intent and decides the operation and the fields it needs. "Into a free centre" aims at a target that does not exist yet, so it needs a free `tabsNodeId` and a `home`; `tab-into` needs neither. Overloaded, one kind would map to two operations, and a `tab-into` preview aimed at an edge-zone would pass validation and fail in the reducer. The name is the document's own word (`zones.center`, `slot: 'center'`).

**Tier: the model contract, as you read it.** The kind row (`:390`) and the conversion table (`:415`) gain one entry each. A third line belongs there: `placement.tabsNodeId` in the field table. The preview payload is runtime only, so `neo.dock.zone.v1` is untouched.

**The lock.** `zone-center → restoreTab` moves an item that still lives in the tree. `restoreTab` (`Operations.mjs:238`) has no lock check, and its dispatch entry (`:46`) does not take the `addTab → moveItem` downgrade (`:41-44`) that carries the guard for every `tab-*` drop (`:359`). The ADR's lock amendment makes the reducer "the independent boundary for stale chrome and programmatic descriptors". So:

- `restoreTab` rejects an item that is in the tree **and** locked. A returning pane is not in the tree, so the return of `#21375` is untouched.
- One unit arm: a `zone-center` drop of a locked in-tree item fails closed and leaves the document as it was.
- This is not new with your ticket: since `#21830` the same descriptor is reachable programmatically on `dev`. Your pull request closes it.

**That makes the impact `amends`, by one clause.** The ADR's lock paragraph lists the operations that enforce the rule, and the list has to stay true: "`closeItem`, `detachItem`, source `moveItem`, and `restoreTab` for an item still in the tree reject a locked item at the model boundary *(amendment, 2026-11-22 — #21827)*". It can ride your pull request in this wording.

**Visible behaviour: agreed on all three.** The whole well as the region; no five-position menu, because there is nothing to split against; no preview for a whole stack. The well's line names the pane that is away and promises no drop, so a stack that finds no target contradicts nothing. One look criterion: over the well the preview uses the fill of a `tab-into` preview over a stack, so that a user reads "into here" and not a new kind of zone. One dark frame of the well under a drag is my look read.
